mara_voss:after_defeat: Our battle ended once. The log has two finishing times. I kept the video; could you check the original record at the training field?
How far apart are the times?
Is there a cut in the video?
I will compare the record with your video.
One second. A confirmation was sent before the battle actually ended.
No. I watched it again; it runs continuously from the opening to the end.
Good. Keep the originals. Do not change the times just to make them match.
mara_voss:after_echo: I kept another copy of the video. Hale wants to compare Orin's records; I can send my part when they need it.
Did you see anyone change the log?
Could you send Orin the video directly?
I will keep the copies as they are.
No. I saw a discrepancy. I am not naming someone without evidence.
Yes. Tell me when Orin has the file and I will send the camera's timestamps too.
Right. Note the differences separately; do not erase a copy.
dr_orin:after_defeat: I copied the records we need to compare. Rook has a Black Card tied to an old access entry. We need to examine both.
Does the card prove who accessed the system?
I will examine the card before drawing a conclusion.
Not yet. It proves access was available. Its current holder may not be the person who used it.
Where he obtained it and when. If those answers conflict, preserve both.
Exactly. An object does not explain how it was used.
dr_orin:after_archive: The comparison is saved separately. The file's administrative labels do not prove its account of events is accurate.
I will bring both the original and the comparison.
Yes. Include the source and copying date so the reader can identify the version.
Unrelated people's personal information. We need evidence of these events, not their entire lives.
Good. That lets someone check how we reached our conclusions.
rook:after_defeat: You have the Black Card. I kept the receipt. Show Selene the card before asking about its confirmation mark.
I will ask her about the mark.
To prove I bought it rather than made it. Those are different, even if you dislike the seller.
She can read the mark. Whether she recognizes its user is a question for her.
Fine. If she disagrees with me, send her exact words. I dislike being quoted halfway.
rook:after_card: Marlow wants to compare the card with Iris's lab records. I handed over the receipt; ask the records' keeper about the rest.
Did you keep a copy of the receipt?
Why do we need Iris's records?
Yes. This time I noted the handover date too, so we need not argue about who sent what first.
I know how the card was sold. Iris knows how it was used in the laboratory.
Ask me about the sale. Do not make me answer for her about the lab.
selene_kade:after_defeat: I recorded the card's confirmation mark. The Town 5 Wardens keep some area-access records; compare it with theirs.
What should I bring to the Wardens?
I will ask them about that access entry.
Yes. That is why I recorded where and when it appeared, not just its shape.
The card copy and these notes. Show both before naming a suspect.
All right. If they do not remember, do not press them to choose a name.
selene_kade:after_stalemate: Rocket has reportedly taken the Town 6 lab. Iris is still there. I am checking a way to reach her.
How can I help keep contact?
I will check whether Iris is safe.
The blocked entrance is confirmed. I do not yet know everyone still inside.
Keep your phone on. If you reach Iris, let her speak directly rather than passing her account through several people.
Be careful. Her safety comes first; the records come after that.
aurelia:after_defeat: Your result has been recorded. Bran keeps the School of Wolf files; I will send him the confirmation you need.
What does Bran know about this file?
Must I repeat the League challenge?
I will meet Bran with the confirmation.
He knows the school's intake and storage procedures. I will answer for decisions made by the League.
No. Your result stands. We are handling records, not changing the battle outcome.
If the school needs to verify my signature, ask them to contact me directly.
aurelia:after_below: I sent the copy to the school. Its trials are the school's responsibility; they cannot replace my explanation of the old decisions.
Who should I ask about the trials?
Will the old files remain intact?
I will keep competition separate from the investigation.
Bran receives visitors and can direct you to each trial's examiner.
Yes. Add corrections separately. Do not rewrite the old file as though the mistaken decision never existed.
Thank you. I must make the same distinction when I answer the investigators.
mysterious:first_contact: I saw the record you brought Hale. The early confirmation is not the field clock's fault. I kept an older copy for comparison.
Where did you obtain that record?
How can I check your older copy?
I will compare it, but I am not taking your word for it.
I once had access to those files. I will include the source information so you need not trust a message alone.
Keep your copy and ask Orin to read the confirmation timestamps. Compare signatures as well as times when you receive mine.
That is fair. I want the record examined, not your agreement before you see it.
mysterious:you_are_asking: Orin has compared the confirmation. You are looking in the right place. I still have the old access copy.
Why have you not handed it over yet?
I will record the unresolved differences.
The timestamps match. We need Rook's card to interpret the signature and access rights fully.
Its chain of custody needs recording. Without a source, someone could call it a newly inserted copy.
Record what matches too, when you compare it with mine.
mysterious:last_person: The group has been told about the archive. I want to meet after you read it. There are things I must explain myself.
Which parts should I read first?
Will you explain how you used us too?
I will read the files before agreeing to meet.
The old order, Selene's copy and Iris's account. Read them together, not just the part bearing my name.
Yes. I used your investigation to reopen access. I will not leave that out.
All right. I will send the meeting point through this conversation.
mysterious:meet_me: The meeting point is on your phone. Keep the records you compared. I will answer in front of them, not ask you to leave them behind.
May I tell the group where we are meeting?
Do I need to return the files to you?
I will come and keep the comparison copies.
Yes. I want witnesses. You need not hide the meeting from everyone.
No. Keep them. If I need to see an entry, we can read it there.
Keep them with you while we talk.
mysterious:first_contact_who: I am not giving my name in this message. Check the old access rights first; they left a trace in the file.
Will you let Orin examine it?
I will check the trace before asking more.
At the confirmation dated before the training field opened. Keep the surrounding lines so its source can be checked.
Yes. I want someone holding an independent copy to read it with you.
Point to whatever still does not match when you ask again.
mysterious:first_contact_what: I want you to preserve the original and compare it with Orin's records. That is my request; it does not commit you to anything else.
What if the copies do not match?
May I show this copy to Hale?
I agree to check the record.
Record the differences. Do not edit either copy; we need to know when each discrepancy appeared.
Yes. He already received part of it and can examine its source.
You can stop if my account contradicts the file.
mysterious:first_contact_why: Part of the file treats a former access holder as a fabrication. I need that checked against older records, rather than accepted because it is already written down.
Is there evidence against that conclusion?
Do you want us to erase the old conclusion?
I will examine the evidence first.
An access right predates the account's recorded creation. Orin can help verify those times.
No. Keep it so we can see who concluded that and why. A mistake needs an explanation, not an erased trace.
I will provide my copy for comparison.
